card.name: Drug name subject before a verb
card.fires_on: The end of a drug name used as sentence subject, or the comma after it, right where a verb such as can cause or increase comes next. Seen in warnings and adverse reaction headings.

modes.label: Drug name then can
modes.description: The word can, or the last piece of a brand name, just before can cause a reaction.
modes.example: Hypophysitis TECENTRIQ<< can>> cause immune-mediated hypophysitis.

modes.label: Comma after drug phrase
modes.description: A comma closing a drug name or qualifier before the main statement about the drug.
modes.example: Thiazolidinediones, including pioglitazone<<,>> which is a component of alogli

modes.label: Drug then effect verb
modes.description: A verb like increase right after the drug name in interaction text.
modes.example: Imatinib mesylate tablets<< increase>> the mean C max and AUC of

card.writes: It pushes toward verbs and words that follow a drug subject, though the listed tokens are mixed and unclear.
card.plain: It marks the spot right after a drug's name where the sentence says what the drug does.
